ESV.1: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said before Jonathan, “What have I done? What is my guilt? And what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?”
ESV.2: And he said to him, “Far from it! You shall not die. Behold, my father does nothing either great or small without disclosing it to me. And why should my father hide this from me? It is not so.”
ESV.3: But David vowed again, saying, “Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he thinks, ‘Do not let Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved.’ But truly, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death.”
ESV.4: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you say, I will do for you.”
ESV.5: David said to Jonathan, “Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should not fail to sit at table with the king. But let me go, that I may hide myself in the field till the third day at evening.
ESV.6: If your father misses me at all, then say, ‘David earnestly asked leave of me to run to Bethlehem his city, for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the clan.’
ESV.7: If he says, ‘Good!’ it will be well with your servant, but if he is angry, then know that harm is determined by him.
ESV.8: Therefore deal kindly with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. But if there is guilt in me, kill me yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?”
ESV.9: And Jonathan said, “Far be it from you! If I knew that it was determined by my father that harm should come to you, would I not tell you?”
ESV.10: Then David said to Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you roughly?”
ESV.11: And Jonathan said to David, “Come, let us go out into the field.” So they both went out into the field.
ESV.12: And Jonathan said to David, “The LORD, the God of Israel, be witness!  When I have sounded out my father, about this time tomorrow, or the third day, behold, if he is well disposed toward David, shall I not then send and disclose it to you?
ESV.13: But should it please my father to do you harm, the LORD do so to Jonathan and more also if I do not disclose it to you and send you away, that you may go in safety. May the LORD be with you, as he has been with my father.
ESV.14: If I am still alive, show me the steadfast love of the LORD, that I may not die;
ESV.15: and do not cut off  your steadfast love from my house forever, when the LORD cuts off every one of the enemies of David from the face of the earth.”
ESV.16: And Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May  the LORD take vengeance on David's enemies.”
ESV.17: And Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
ESV.18: Then Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
ESV.19: On the third day go down quickly to the place where you hid yourself when the matter was in hand, and remain beside the stone heap.
ESV.20: And I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I shot at a mark.
ESV.21: And behold, I will send the boy, saying, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you, take them,’ then you are to come, for, as the LORD lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.
ESV.22: But if I say to the youth, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then go, for the LORD has sent you away.
ESV.23: And as for the matter of which you and I have spoken, behold, the LORD is between you and me forever.”
ESV.24: So David hid himself in the field. And when the new moon came, the king sat down to eat food.
ESV.25: The king sat on his seat, as at other times, on the seat by the wall. Jonathan sat opposite,  and Abner sat by Saul's side, but David's place was empty.

ESV.27: But on the second day, the day after the new moon, David's place was empty. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, “Why has not the son of Jesse come to the meal, either yesterday or today?”
ESV.28: Jonathan answered Saul, “David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Bethlehem.

ESV.31: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Therefore send and bring him to me, for he shall surely die.”
ESV.32: Then Jonathan answered Saul his father, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
ESV.33: But Saul hurled his spear at him to strike him. So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to put David to death.
ESV.34: And Jonathan rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for David, because his father had disgraced him.

ESV.36: And he said to his boy, “Run and find the arrows that I shoot.” As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
ESV.37: And when the boy came to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called after the boy and said, “Is not the arrow beyond you?”
ESV.38: And Jonathan called after the boy, “Hurry! Be quick! Do not stay!” So Jonathan's boy gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
ESV.39: But the boy knew nothing. Only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
ESV.40: And Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, “Go and carry them to the city.”
ESV.41: And as soon as the boy had gone, David rose from beside the stone heap  and fell on his face to the ground and bowed three times. And they kissed one another and wept with one another, David weeping the most.
ESV.42: Then Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, because we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘The LORD shall be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, forever.’” And he rose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.

NASB.1: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said to Jonathan, 'What have I done? What is my iniquity? And what is my sin before your father, that he is seeking my life?'
NASB.2: He said to him, 'Far from it, you shall not die. Behold, my father does nothing either great or small without disclosing it to me. So why should my father hide this thing from me? It is not so!'
NASB.3: Yet David vowed again, saying, 'Your father knows well that I have found favor in your sight, and he has said, 'Do not let Jonathan know this, or he will be grieved.' But truly as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is hardly a step between me and death.'
NASB.4: Then Jonathan said to David, 'Whatever you say, I will do for you.'
NASB.5: So David said to Jonathan, 'Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I ought to sit down to eat with the king. But let me go, that I may hide myself in the field until the third evening.
NASB.6: 'If your father misses me at all, then say, 'David earnestly asked [leave] of me to run to Bethlehem his city, because it is the yearly sacrifice there for the whole family.'
NASB.7: 'If he says, 'It is good,' your servant [will be] safe; but if he is very angry, know that he has decided on evil.
NASB.8: 'Therefore deal kindly with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. But if there is iniquity in me, put me to death yourself; for why then should you bring me to your father?'
NASB.9: Jonathan said, 'Far be it from you! For if I should indeed learn that evil has been decided by my father to come upon you, then would I not tell you about it?'
NASB.10: Then David said to Jonathan, 'Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?'
NASB.11: Jonathan said to David, 'Come, and let us go out into the field.' So both of them went out to the field.
NASB.12: Then Jonathan said to David, 'The LORD, the God of Israel, [be witness]! When I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, [or] the third day, behold, if there is good [feeling] toward David, shall I not then send to you and make it known to you?
NASB.13: 'If it please my father [to do] you harm, may the LORD do so to Jonathan and more also, if I do not make it known to you and send you away, that you may go in safety. And may the LORD be with you as He has been with my father.
NASB.14: 'If I am still alive, will you not show me the lovingkindness of the LORD, that I may not die?
NASB.15: 'You shall not cut off your lovingkindness from my house forever, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of the enemies of David from the face of the earth.'
NASB.16: So Jonathan made a [covenant] with the house of David, [saying], 'May the LORD require [it] at the hands of David's enemies.'
NASB.17: Jonathan made David vow again because of his love for him, because he loved him as he loved his own life.
NASB.18: Then Jonathan said to him, 'Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed because your seat will be empty.
NASB.19: 'When you have stayed for three days, you shall go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself on that eventful day, and you shall remain by the stone Ezel.
NASB.20: 'I will shoot three arrows to the side, as though I shot at a target.
NASB.21: 'And behold, I will send the lad, [saying], 'Go, find the arrows.' If I specifically say to the lad, 'Behold, the arrows are on this side of you, get them,' then come; for there is safety for you and no harm, as the LORD lives.
NASB.22: 'But if I say to the youth, 'Behold, the arrows are beyond you,' go, for the LORD has sent you away.
NASB.23: 'As for the agreement of which you and I have spoken, behold, the LORD is between you and me forever.'
NASB.24: So David hid in the field; and when the new moon came, the king sat down to eat food.
NASB.25: The king sat on his seat as usual, the seat by the wall; then Jonathan rose up and Abner sat down by Saul's side, but David's place was empty.
NASB.26: Nevertheless Saul did not speak anything that day, for he thought, 'It is an accident, he is not clean, surely [he is] not clean.'
NASB.27: It came about the next day, the second [day] of the new moon, that David's place was empty; so Saul said to Jonathan his son, 'Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?'
NASB.28: Jonathan then answered Saul, 'David earnestly asked leave of me [to go] to Bethlehem,
NASB.29: for he said, 'Please let me go, since our family has a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has commanded me to attend. And now, if I have found favor in your sight, please let me get away that I may see my brothers.' For this reason he has not come to the king's table.'
NASB.30: Then Saul's anger burned against Jonathan and he said to him, 'You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you are choosing the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?
NASB.31: 'For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. Therefore now, send and bring him to me, for he must surely die.'
NASB.32: But Jonathan answered Saul his father and said to him, 'Why should he be put to death? What has he done?'
NASB.33: Then Saul hurled his spear at him to strike him down; so Jonathan knew that his father had decided to put David to death.
NASB.34: Then Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did not eat food on the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved over David because his father had dishonored him.
NASB.35: Now it came about in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field for the appointment with David, and a little lad [was] with him.
NASB.36: He said to his lad, 'Run, find now the arrows which I am about to shoot.' As the lad was running, he shot an arrow past him.
NASB.37: When the lad reached the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called after the lad and said, 'Is not the arrow beyond you?'
NASB.38: And Jonathan called after the lad, 'Hurry, be quick, do not stay!' And Jonathan's lad picked up the arrow and came to his master.
NASB.39: But the lad was not aware of anything; only Jonathan and David knew about the matter.
NASB.40: Then Jonathan gave his weapons to his lad and said to him, 'Go, bring [them] to the city.'
NASB.41: When the lad was gone, David rose from the south side and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed three times. And they kissed each other and wept together, but David [wept] the more.
NASB.42: Jonathan said to David, 'Go in safety, inasmuch as we have sworn to each other in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD will be between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants forever.'' Then he rose and departed, while Jonathan went into the city.

NLT.1: David now fled from Naioth in Ramah and found Jonathan. “What have I done?” he exclaimed. “What is my crime? How have I offended your father that he is so determined to kill me?”
NLT.2: “That’s not true!” Jonathan protested. “You’re not going to die. He always tells me everything he’s going to do, even the little things. I know my father wouldn’t hide something like this from me. It just isn’t so!”
NLT.3: Then David took an oath before Jonathan and said, “Your father knows perfectly well about our friendship, so he has said to himself, ‘I won’t tell Jonathan — why should I hurt him?’ But I swear to you that I am only a step away from death! I swear it by the LORD and by your own soul!”
NLT.4: “Tell me what I can do to help you,” Jonathan exclaimed.
NLT.5: David replied, “Tomorrow we celebrate the new moon festival. I’ve always eaten with the king on this occasion, but tomorrow I’ll hide in the field and stay there until the evening of the third day.
NLT.6: If your father asks where I am, tell him I asked permission to go home to Bethlehem for an annual family sacrifice.
NLT.7: If he says, ‘Fine!’ you will know all is well. But if he is angry and loses his temper, you will know he is determined to kill me.
NLT.8: Show me this loyalty as my sworn friend — for we made a solemn pact before the LORD — or kill me yourself if I have sinned against your father. But please don’t betray me to him!”
NLT.9: “Never!” Jonathan exclaimed. “You know that if I had the slightest notion my father was planning to kill you, I would tell you at once.”
NLT.10: Then David asked, “How will I know whether or not your father is angry?”
NLT.11: “Come out to the field with me,” Jonathan replied. And they went out there together.
NLT.12: Then Jonathan told David, “I promise by the LORD, the God of Israel, that by this time tomorrow, or the next day at the latest, I will talk to my father and let you know at once how he feels about you. If he speaks favorably about you, I will let you know.
NLT.13: But if he is angry and wants you killed, may the LORD strike me and even kill me if I don’t warn you so you can escape and live. May the LORD be with you as he used to be with my father.
NLT.14: And may you treat me with the faithful love of the LORD as long as I live. But if I die,
NLT.15: treat my family with this faithful love, even when the LORD destroys all your enemies from the face of the earth.”
NLT.16: So Jonathan made a solemn pact with David, saying, “May the LORD destroy all your enemies!”
NLT.17: And Jonathan made David reaffirm his vow of friendship again, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
NLT.18: Then Jonathan said, “Tomorrow we celebrate the new moon festival. You will be missed when your place at the table is empty.
NLT.19: The day after tomorrow, toward evening, go to the place where you hid before, and wait there by the stone pile.
NLT.20: I will come out and shoot three arrows to the side of the stone pile as though I were shooting at a target.
NLT.21: Then I will send a boy to bring the arrows back. If you hear me tell him, ‘They’re on this side,’ then you will know, as surely as the LORD lives, that all is well, and there is no trouble.
NLT.22: But if I tell him, ‘Go farther — the arrows are still ahead of you,’ then it will mean that you must leave immediately, for the LORD is sending you away.
NLT.23: And may the LORD make us keep our promises to each other, for he has witnessed them.”
NLT.24: So David hid himself in the field, and when the new moon festival began, the king sat down to eat.
NLT.25: He sat at his usual place against the wall, with Jonathan sitting opposite him and Abner beside him. But David’s place was empty.
NLT.26: Saul didn’t say anything about it that day, for he said to himself, “Something must have made David ceremonially unclean.”
NLT.27: But when David’s place was empty again the next day, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse been here for the meal either yesterday or today?”
NLT.28: Jonathan replied, “David earnestly asked me if he could go to Bethlehem.
NLT.29: He said, ‘Please let me go, for we are having a family sacrifice. My brother demanded that I be there. So please let me get away to see my brothers.’ That’s why he isn’t here at the king’s table.”
NLT.30: Saul boiled with rage at Jonathan. “You stupid son of a whore!” he swore at him. “Do you think I don’t know that you want him to be king in your place, shaming yourself and your mother?
NLT.31: As long as that son of Jesse is alive, you’ll never be king. Now go and get him so I can kill him!”
NLT.32: “But why should he be put to death?” Jonathan asked his father. “What has he done?”
NLT.33: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan, intending to kill him. So at last Jonathan realized that his father was really determined to kill David.
NLT.34: Jonathan left the table in fierce anger and refused to eat on that second day of the festival, for he was crushed by his father’s shameful behavior toward David.
NLT.35: The next morning, as agreed, Jonathan went out into the field and took a young boy with him to gather his arrows.
NLT.36: “Start running,” he told the boy, “so you can find the arrows as I shoot them.” So the boy ran, and Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
NLT.37: When the boy had almost reached the arrow, Jonathan shouted, “The arrow is still ahead of you.
NLT.38: Hurry, hurry, don’t wait.” So the boy quickly gathered up the arrows and ran back to his master.
NLT.39: He, of course, suspected nothing; only Jonathan and David understood the signal.
NLT.40: Then Jonathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and told him to take them back to town.
NLT.41: As soon as the boy was gone, David came out from where he had been hiding near the stone pile. Then David bowed three times to Jonathan with his face to the ground. Both of them were in tears as they embraced each other and said good-bye, especially David.
NLT.42: At last Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for we have sworn loyalty to each other in the LORD’s name. The LORD is the witness of a bond between us and our children forever.” Then David left, and Jonathan returned to the town.

NET.3: Taking an oath, David again said, “Your father is very much aware of the fact that I have found favor with you, and he has thought, ‘Don’t let Jonathan know about this, or he will be upset.’ But as surely as the LORD lives and you live, there is about one step between me and death!”
NET.4: Jonathan replied to David, “Tell me what I can do for you.”
NET.5: David said to Jonathan, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and I am certainly expected to join the king for a meal. You must send me away so I can hide in the field until the third evening from now.
NET.6: If your father happens to miss me, you should say, ‘David urgently requested me to let him go to his city Bethlehem, for there is an annual sacrifice there for his entire family.’
NET.7: If he should then say, ‘That’s fine,’ then your servant is safe. But if he becomes very angry, be assured that he has decided to harm me.
NET.8: You must be loyal to your servant, for you have made a covenant with your servant in the LORD’s name. If I am guilty, you yourself kill me! Why bother taking me to your father?”
NET.9: Jonathan said, “Far be it from you to suggest this! If I were at all aware that my father had decided to harm you, wouldn’t I tell you about it?”
NET.10: David said to Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
NET.11: Jonathan said to David, “Come on. Let’s go out to the field.” When the two of them had gone out into the field,
NET.12: Jonathan said to David, “The LORD God of Israel is my witness. I will feel out my father about this time the day after tomorrow. If he is favorably inclined toward David, will I not then send word to you and let you know?
NET.13: But if my father intends to do you harm, may the LORD do all this and more to Jonathan, if I don’t let you know and send word to you so you can go safely on your way. May the LORD be with you, as he was with my father.
NET.14: While I am still alive, extend to me the loyalty of the LORD, or else I will die!
NET.15: Don’t ever cut off your loyalty to my family, not even when the LORD has cut off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth
NET.16: and called David’s enemies to account.” So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David.
NET.17: Jonathan once again took an oath with David, because he loved him. In fact Jonathan loved him as much as he did his own life.
NET.18: Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, for your seat will be empty.
NET.19: On the third day you should go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself the day this all started. Stay near the stone Ezel.
NET.20: I will shoot three arrows near it, as though I were shooting at a target.
NET.21: When I send a boy after them, I will say, “Go and find the arrows.” If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; get them,’ then come back. For as surely as the LORD lives, you will be safe and there will no problem.
NET.22: But if I say to the boy, “Look, the arrows are on the other side of you,’ get away. For in that case the LORD has sent you away.
NET.23: With regard to the matter that you and I discussed, the LORD is the witness between us forever!”
NET.24: So David hid in the field. When the new moon came, the king sat down to eat his meal.
NET.25: The king sat down in his usual place by the wall, with Jonathan opposite him and Abner at his side. But David’s place was vacant.
NET.26: However, Saul said nothing about it that day, for he thought, “Something has happened to make him ceremonially unclean. Yes, he must be unclean.”
NET.27: But the next morning, the second day of the new moon, David’s place was still vacant. So Saul said to his son Jonathan, “Why has Jesse’s son not come to the meal yesterday or today?”
NET.28: Jonathan replied to Saul, “David urgently requested that he be allowed to go to Bethlehem.
NET.29: He said, ‘Permit me to go, for we are having a family sacrifice in the city, and my brother urged me to be there. So now, if I have found favor with you, let me go to see my brothers.’ For that reason he has not come to the king’s table.”
NET.30: Saul became angry with Jonathan and said to him, “You stupid traitor! Don’t I realize that to your own disgrace and to the disgrace of your mother’s nakedness you have chosen this son of Jesse?
NET.31: For as long as this son of Jesse is alive on the earth, you and your kingdom will not be established. Now, send some men and bring him to me. For he is as good as dead!”
NET.32: Jonathan responded to his father Saul, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
NET.33: Then Saul threw his spear at Jonathan in order to strike him down. So Jonathan was convinced that his father had decided to kill David.
NET.34: Jonathan got up from the table enraged. He did not eat any food on that second day of the new moon, for he was upset that his father had humiliated David.
NET.35: The next morning Jonathan, along with a young servant, went out to the field to meet David.
NET.36: He said to his servant, “Run, find the arrows that I am about to shoot.” As the servant ran, Jonathan shot the arrow beyond him.
NET.37: When the servant came to the place where Jonathan had shot the arrow, Jonathan called out to the servant, “Isn’t the arrow further beyond you?”
NET.38: Jonathan called out to the servant, “Hurry! Go faster! Don’t delay!” Jonathan’s servant retrieved the arrow and came back to his master.
NET.39: (Now the servant did not understand any of this. Only Jonathan and David knew what was going on.)
NET.40: Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the servant who was with him. He said to him, “Go, take these things back to the city.”
NET.41: When the servant had left, David got up from beside the mound, knelt with his face to the ground, and bowed three times. Then they kissed each other and they both wept, especially David.
NET.42: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn together in the name of the LORD saying, ‘The LORD will be between me and you and between my descendants and your descendants forever.’”
